lines.title: Sveshnikov: 5...e5 Main Line
lines.pgn: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 e5 6. Ndb5 d6 7. Bg5 a6 8. Na3 b5 9. Nd5 Be7 10. Bxf6 Bxf6 11. c3
lines.lineSummary: The Sveshnikov — Black plays ...e5 accepting a backward d6 pawn for active piece play and the d5 square.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...e5 to gain space. Accept the d6 weakness in exchange for active pieces and ...d5 break potential.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Nd5 too early without Bxf6, allowing Black to maintain the bishop pair.
lines.punishmentIdea: If White doesn't exchange on f6, Black keeps the bishop pair and plays ...Be7-g5 with activity.
lines.hintText: In the Sveshnikov, ...e5 is the key move. The d5 square is yours — use it!

lines.title: Taimanov: 4...e6 5.Nc3 a6
lines.pgn: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nc6 5. Nc3 a6 6. Be2 Nge7 7. O-O Nxd4 8. Qxd4 Nc6 9. Qd3 b5
lines.lineSummary: The Taimanov — a flexible Sicilian where Black keeps options open with ...e6 and ...a6.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...e6 and ...a6 for maximum flexibility. Can transpose to Scheveningen or Hedgehog structures.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Be3 too early, allowing ...Nxd4 Bxd4 e5 winning a tempo on the bishop.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Nxd4 Bxd4 e5, the bishop must retreat and Black gains central space.
lines.hintText: The Taimanov is about flexibility. ...a6 prepares ...b5 and keeps all Sicilian structures available.

lines.title: Kan: 4...a6 Hedgehog
lines.pgn: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 a6 5. Nc3 b5 6. Bd3 Qb6 7. Nf3 Bb7 8. O-O Nc6 9. Re1 Bc5
lines.lineSummary: The Kan/Paulsen — Black plays ...a6 immediately, aiming for a Hedgehog or ...b5 expansion.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...a6 and ...b5 for queenside expansion. Develop ...Bb7 and aim for a Hedgehog setup.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays too aggressively without securing the center, allowing ...b5-b4 with tempo.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...b5-b4, White's Nc3 is displaced and Black gets queenside initiative.
lines.hintText: The Kan is flexible — ...a6 prepares ...b5 and you can choose between Hedgehog or ...d5 break.

lines.title: Accelerated Dragon: 4...g6
lines.pgn: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 g6 5. Nc3 Bg7 6. Be3 Nf6 7. Bc4 O-O 8. Bb3 d6 9. f3 Bd7
lines.lineSummary: The Accelerated Dragon — Black fianchettoes without ...d6 first, avoiding the Yugoslav Attack.
lines.strategicGoal: Fianchetto immediately with ...g6 to avoid the Yugoslav Attack. Aim for ...d5 in one move.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays the Yugoslav Attack setup, but without ...d6, Black can play ...d5 in one go.
lines.punishmentIdea: Without ...d6, Black can play ...d7-d5 in one move, equalizing the center immediately.
lines.hintText: The Accelerated Dragon avoids the Yugoslav Attack. Your key idea is ...d5 in one move!

lines.title: vs Smith-Morra Gambit: Declined
lines.pgn: 1. e4 c5 2. d4 cxd4 3. c3 d3 4. Bxd3 d6 5. Nf3 Nf6 6. O-O g6 7. Nc3 Bg7 8. Bf4 O-O
lines.lineSummary: Against the Smith-Morra Gambit, Black declines with ...d3! — the simplest and safest response.
lines.strategicGoal: Decline the gambit with ...d3! After Bxd3, develop normally. Black is a tempo up effectively.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Bxd3 and has a slightly passive position without the gambit compensation.
lines.punishmentIdea: By declining with ...d3, Black avoids all the Morra's tactical tricks and gets a comfortable game.
lines.hintText: Against the Smith-Morra (2.d4 cxd4 3.c3), play ...d3! Decline the gambit for a safe edge.

lines.title: vs Grand Prix Attack: f4
lines.pgn: 1. e4 c5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. f4 g6 4. Nf3 Bg7 5. Bb5 Nd4 6. O-O Nxb5 7. Nxb5 d5 8. exd5 a6 9. Nc3 Nf6
lines.lineSummary: Against the Grand Prix Attack (f4), Black plays ...g6 and ...Bg7 for a solid Dragon-like setup.
lines.strategicGoal: Fianchetto with ...g6 and ...Bg7. After ...Nd4, exchange the annoying Bb5 and play ...d5.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Bb5 but after ...Nd4, the bishop must be exchanged or retreat.
lines.punishmentIdea: ...Nd4 forces Nxb5 or bishop retreat. Either way, Black gets ...d5 with equality.
lines.hintText: Against the Grand Prix (f4), fianchetto and play ...Nd4 to challenge the Bb5.

lines.title: Scheveningen: ...e6 ...d6 Setup
lines.pgn: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 e6 6. Be2 Be7 7. O-O O-O 8. f4 Nc6 9. Be3 a6
lines.lineSummary: The Scheveningen — Black's small center (...e6 + ...d6) is flexible and supports counterplay.
lines.strategicGoal: Build a compact center with ...e6 and ...d6. Prepare ...b5 queenside expansion or ...d5 break.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White pushes f5 too early without preparation, allowing ...e5 with a strong center.
lines.punishmentIdea: After premature f5, ...e5 gives Black a great center and the f5 pawn becomes weak.
lines.hintText: The Scheveningen is about flexibility. Your center is small but solid — wait for the right ...d5 or ...b5.

lines.title: vs Rossolimo: 3.Bb5
lines.pgn: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 g6 4. O-O Bg7 5. Re1 e5 6. Bxc6 dxc6 7. d3 Qe7 8. Nbd2 Nf6 9. Nc4
lines.lineSummary: Against the Rossolimo (3.Bb5), Black plays ...g6 and accepts doubled c-pawns for the bishop pair.
lines.strategicGoal: After Bxc6 dxc6, use the bishop pair and central pawns. ...e5 gives a strong center.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White exchanges on c6 too early, giving Black the bishop pair without compensation.
lines.punishmentIdea: After dxc6, Black has the bishop pair and strong center. The doubled c-pawns control d5 and b5.
lines.hintText: Against the Rossolimo, ...g6 is the main response. Accept doubled pawns — the bishop pair compensates.

lines.title: O'Kelly: 2...a6 Surprise
lines.pgn: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 a6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 e5 6. Nb3 Bb4 7. Bd3 d5 8. exd5 O-O
lines.lineSummary: The O'Kelly variation — ...a6 on move 2 is a flexible surprise weapon avoiding main lines.
lines.strategicGoal: ...a6 prevents Bb5 and keeps options open. Can transpose to many Sicilian structures.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays d4 without preparation, allowing Black to get a favorable Sicilian structure.
lines.punishmentIdea: After d4 cxd4 Nxd4, Black has avoided all Anti-Sicilians and gets a good Open Sicilian.
lines.hintText: 2...a6 is a surprise weapon. It prevents Bb5 and forces White into the Open Sicilian on your terms.

lines.title: Trap: Siberian Trap (Alapin)
lines.pgn: 1. e4 c5 2. c3 d5 3. exd5 Qxd5 4. d4 Nf6 5. Nf3 Bg4 6. Be2 e6 7. O-O Nc6 8. h3 Bh5 9. Be3 cxd4 10. cxd4 Bb4
lines.lineSummary: The Siberian Trap in the Alapin — Black sets up a tactical shot winning material.
lines.strategicGoal: Develop with ...Bg4 and ...Nc6, then after ...cxd4 cxd4, play ...Bb4 threatening ...Nxd4.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays h3 and cxd4 without seeing the ...Bb4 and ...Nxd4 tactical combination.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Bb4, if White plays a3, ...Qa5! pins. If not, ...Nxd4 wins the d-pawn.
lines.hintText: In the Alapin, set up ...Bg4, ...Nc6, then ...cxd4 cxd4 ...Bb4 — a nasty tactical trick.

lines.title: Orthodox: ...Be7 Main Line
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 Nbd7 7. Rc1 c6 8. Bd3 dxc4 9. Bxc4 Nd5
lines.lineSummary: The Orthodox QGD — Black's most solid and time-tested defense. Capablanca's favorite.
lines.strategicGoal: Develop solidly with ...Be7, ...O-O, ...Nbd7. Then break with ...c5 or ...dxc4 followed by ...Nd5.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays e4 too early without preparation, allowing ...dxe4 Nxe4 Nxe4 with equality.
lines.punishmentIdea: After premature e4, ...dxe4 Nxe4 Nxe4 Bxe7 Qxe7 equalizes completely.
lines.hintText: The Orthodox QGD is rock-solid. Develop ...Be7, ...O-O, ...Nbd7, then choose ...c5 or ...dxc4.

lines.title: Ragozin: 4...Bb4
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 Bb4 5. Bg5 h6 6. Bxf6 Qxf6 7. e3 O-O 8. Rc1 dxc4 9. Bxc4 c5 10. O-O cxd4
lines.lineSummary: The Ragozin — Black pins Nc3 with ...Bb4, combining QGD solidity with Nimzo-Indian ideas.
lines.strategicGoal: Pin Nc3 with ...Bb4 to create pressure. After ...h6 Bxf6 Qxf6, Black has the bishop pair.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Bg5 and is forced to exchange after ...h6, giving Black the bishop pair.
lines.punishmentIdea: After Bxf6 Qxf6, Black has the bishop pair and can play ...c5 to open the position.
lines.hintText: The Ragozin (...Bb4) combines the best of QGD and Nimzo-Indian. You get the bishop pair!

lines.title: Vienna Variation: 4...dxc4
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 dxc4 5. e4 Bb4 6. Bg5 c5 7. Bxc4 cxd4 8. Nxd4 Qa5 9. Bd2 Qc5
lines.lineSummary: The Vienna Variation — Black takes on c4 early and plays ...Bb4 for active counterplay.
lines.strategicGoal: Take on c4 to provoke e4, then pin with ...Bb4 and play ...c5 to attack White's center.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White pushes e4 but the center becomes overextended after ...c5 and ...cxd4.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...c5 and ...cxd4, White's center collapses and Black gets active piece play.
lines.hintText: 4...dxc4 provokes e4, then ...Bb4 and ...c5 attack the overextended center.

lines.title: Tartakower: ...b6 System
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 h6 7. Bh4 b6 8. Bd3 Bb7 9. O-O Nbd7 10. Bg3 c5
lines.lineSummary: The Tartakower — Black plays ...b6 and ...Bb7 to develop the light-squared bishop actively.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...h6 and ...b6 to fianchetto the bishop. ...Bb7 pressures e4 and supports ...c5 break.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White allows ...c5 without preparation, giving Black easy equality and counterplay.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...c5, the position opens favorably for Black's bishop on b7. The center becomes fluid.
lines.hintText: The Tartakower (...b6) solves the QGD's main problem — the light-squared bishop gets active on b7.

lines.title: Lasker Defense: ...Ne4
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 h6 7. Bh4 Ne4 8. Bxe7 Qxe7 9. Rc1 c6 10. Bd3 Nxc3 11. Rxc3 dxc4 12. Bxc4
lines.lineSummary: The Lasker Defense — Black plays ...Ne4 to exchange pieces and ease the cramped position.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...Ne4 to force exchanges. After Bxe7 Qxe7 and ...Nxc3, Black's position is freed.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White exchanges on e7 and c3, simplifying into a position where Black has no weaknesses.
lines.punishmentIdea: After exchanges, Black has a solid position with no weaknesses. The endgame is comfortable.
lines.hintText: The Lasker Defense (...Ne4) is the great equalizer. Exchange pieces to free your cramped position.

lines.title: Cambridge Springs: ...Qa5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. Nf3 c6 6. e3 Qa5 7. Nd2 Bb4 8. Qc2 O-O 9. Bh4 e5
lines.lineSummary: The Cambridge Springs — Black plays ...Qa5 creating tactical pressure on c3 and g5.
lines.strategicGoal: ...Qa5 attacks Nc3 and pins the Bg5. Combined with ...Bb4, Black creates real threats.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White doesn't see the ...Bb4 pin coming after ...Qa5, losing material.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Qa5 and ...Bb4, the Nc3 is pinned and Bg5 is attacked. White must be very precise.
lines.hintText: The Cambridge Springs (...Qa5) is a tactical weapon. It attacks both Nc3 and threatens ...Bb4.

lines.title: vs Exchange: Minority Attack Defense
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Bg5 Be7 6. e3 O-O 7. Bd3 Nbd7 8. Nf3 Re8 9. Qc2 c6 10. O-O Nf8
lines.lineSummary: Against the Exchange QGD, Black defends the queenside and aims for kingside counterplay.
lines.strategicGoal: After cxd5 exd5, prepare ...Nf8-e6 or ...Ng6 for kingside play. Defend queenside with ...c6.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White's minority attack is slow, allowing Black to generate kingside play with ...Ne4 and ...f5.
lines.punishmentIdea: While White prepares b4-b5, Black plays ...Ne4 and ...f5 for a kingside attack.
lines.hintText: Against the Exchange, play ...Nf8-e6/g6 for kingside activity while defending the queenside with ...c6.

lines.title: Alatortsev: ...a6 System
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 a6 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Bf4 Nf6 6. e3 Bd6 7. Bxd6 Qxd6 8. Bd3 O-O 9. Nf3 c5
lines.lineSummary: The ...a6 system — a modern approach preparing ...b5 and avoiding the main line pin with Bg5.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...a6 to prepare ...b5 expansion and avoid Bg5 pin. Simple development follows.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays cxd5 exd5 too early, giving Black easy development and ...c5 break.
lines.punishmentIdea: After cxd5 exd5, Black develops freely. ...Bd6 and ...c5 equalize comfortably.
lines.hintText: ...a6 is a modern move order trick. It avoids Bg5 and prepares ...b5 queenside expansion.

lines.title: Trap: Elephant Trap (Black wins)
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. cxd5 exd5 6. Nxd5 Nxd5 7. Bxd8 Bb4+ 8. Qd2 Bxd2+ 9. Kxd2 Kxd8
lines.lineSummary: The Elephant Trap from Black's perspective — if White greedily takes on d5, Black wins the queen!
lines.strategicGoal: Set up with ...Nbd7 and after cxd5 exd5, if White plays Nxd5??, ...Bb4+ wins the queen.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Nxd5 thinking they win a pawn, missing the ...Bb4+ discovered attack on the queen.
lines.punishmentIdea: After Nxd5?? Bb4+! Qd2 Bxd2+ Kxd2 Kxd8, Black has won the queen for a bishop.
lines.hintText: Set up the Elephant Trap with ...Nbd7. If White plays Nxd5, ...Bb4+ wins their queen!

lines.title: vs Bf4 System: Active Plan
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 Be7 5. Bf4 O-O 6. e3 c5 7. dxc5 Bxc5 8. Qc2 Nc6 9. a3 Qa5 10. Rd1 Be7
lines.lineSummary: Against the Bf4 system, Black plays ...c5 early to challenge the center and get active play.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...c5 to open the position. After dxc5 Bxc5, develop actively with ...Nc6 and ...Qa5.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays dxc5 giving Black free development and active pieces.
lines.punishmentIdea: After dxc5 Bxc5, Black has rapid development and the bishop is active on c5.
lines.hintText: Against Bf4, play ...c5 early! Don't let White get a comfortable London-style position.
